implementation_notes: The .NET archetype is the AntiPatterns one almost literally: a controller or a `Manager` that holds the domain objects and does the processing, with the objects passive. ASP.NET makes this easy because a controller is the obvious place to put new behaviour and because the model classes default to being data holders. The tooling is good: Visual Studio's analyzer reports class size and member access, and the usage map is practical to build from the symbol table. The extraction is to move behaviour onto the entity/value types and keep the controller as an orchestrator, which is also what makes the controller testable.
idiom_name: controller class with the whole application in it
pitfalls: `[ApiController]` models default to being anemic, so a blob controller is the shape the template produces without anyone deciding it.
Entity Framework entity classes carry validation and serialisation by default, which looks like cohesion and is really framework coupling.
`partial class` splits the file without splitting the responsibility, so the blob becomes invisible to file-size metrics.
